chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Ali ibn Yaqtin who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about shortening the prayer in Mecca, so he said: 'Complete it (the full four rak'ahs), and it is not obligatory, except that I love for you what I love for myself.'

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرِ: Shortening the prayer (praying two rak'ahs instead of four)

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory to shorten prayer in Mecca or should one pray the full four rak'ahs?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Ali ibn Yaqtin inquires of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the ruling of shortening (Qasr) versus completing (Tamm) prayer in Mecca. The Imam clarifies that while completing the four-rak'ah prayer is not obligatory, it is highly recommended (mustahabb), reflecting the general Shia juristic view that the sanctity of the Haram allows for full prayer without the necessity of shortening. The Imam’s personal preference for the shorter form highlights the flexibility within the tradition, where both practices are valid but one is preferred for spiritual humility.
